2.text: lone islands not far from the shore. Access was shut off by a stone wall or

3.text: by wooden palisades. The Reindeer Koryak also prepared fortified places

4.text: at points similar to those mentioned. The herd was gathered together and

5.text: pent up in a corral made of sledges, or it was driven away to far-off pastures.

6.text: The people remained in a chosen place behind the bulwark, ready to hold

7.text: out.¹ Some of the Kamchadal villages were also surrounded by bulwarks of

8.text: stones or earth. On ancient village sites in northwestern Kamchatka I have

9.text: still found the remnants of such bulwarks. They were in the form of a large

10.text: quadrangle, with an entrance from the sea-side. Chukchee stories referring

11.text: to the wars with the Cossacks also mention such fortified strongholds, built by

12.text: the Chukchee. One story mentions that the Reindeer Chukchee fled from the

13.text: Cossacks to a very remote place, and took up their position under a cliff.

14.text: The Cossacks came and climbed the cliffs; then, pushing down heavy stones,

15.text: they broke up the fort and exterminated the people. Some other people

19.text: Cossack Wars. — The Cossacks, as related before, are also called Taˊn˙ñɪt.

23.text: One tale mentions the first impression of the coming of the Cossacks: —

24.text: “When they first, came, our people were very much afraid of them, because they were of
24.note: The comma after "first" is printed on the page (confirmed at 2x) — a printer's error, keyed as set per keying_spec.md §2.14.

25.text: quite unknown appearance. Their whiskers stood out like those of the walrus. Their spear-

26.text: heads were a cubit long, and so broad that they obscured the sun. Their eyes were of iron, round

27.text: and black. All their clothing was of iron. They dug the ground with the butt-ends of their spears,

28.text: like angry reindeer-bucks, inviting our warriors to single combat.”

29.text: According to the Chukchee tales, the Russians treated the natives most

30.text: cruelly, they exterminated the people, and murdered all prisoners; with their

31.text: axes they cleft the men in twain, striking them between the legs; and they

32.text: tore the women in two like dried fish. They would put a prisoner in a sitting

33.text: position. Then they would put a rope around his neck, and the other end

34.text: of this rope they would tie to his membrum virile. After that they would

35.text: poke him in the face with a bar of red-hot iron. The man would bound up,

36.text: and his membrum virile would be torn away.
36.note: mz draft read "memórum", the recognizer's error; the raster (confirmed at 2x) reads "membrum", matching line 34's "membrum virile".
